text: Dorothy lived. <break time="0.8s" /> In the middle of the great Kansas prairies. <break time="0.8s" /> With Uncle Henry and Aunt Em. <break time="0.8s" /> Uncle Henry was a farmer. <break time="0.8s" /> And Aunt Em was his wife. <break time="0.8s" /> Their house was small. <break time="0.8s" /> Because the wood for it. <break time="0.8s" /> Had to be carried by wagon. <break time="0.8s" /> Many miles. <break time="0.8s" /> It had four walls, a floor, and a roof. <break time="0.8s" /> Which made one room. <break time="0.8s" /> In this room there were a rusty cookstove. <break time="0.8s" /> A cupboard for the dishes. <break time="0.8s" /> A table, and some chairs. <break time="0.8s" /> Uncle Henry and Aunt Em had a big bed. <break time="0.8s" /> In one corner. <break time="0.8s" /> And Dorothy had a little bed. <break time="0.8s" /> In another. <break time="0.8s" /> Under the floor. <break time="0.8s" /> There was a small, dark hole. <break time="0.8s" /> That the family called a cyclone cellar. <break time="0.8s" /> The family could go there. <break time="0.8s" /> When one of those great whirlwinds came. <break time="0.8s" /> A trap door in the middle of the floor. <break time="0.8s" /> Led down to it. <break time="0.8s" /> When Dorothy stood in the doorway. <break time="0.8s" /> She could see nothing but the great gray prairie. <break time="0.8s" /> The sun had baked the plowed land. <break time="0.8s" /> Into a gray mass. <break time="0.8s" /> With little cracks. <break time="0.8s" /> Once the house had been painted. <break time="0.8s" /> But now it was as dull and gray. <break time="0.8s" /> As everything else.
